content:
In the world of e-commerce, product photography has become a key element for sales and customer loyalty. Brands need to be able to present their products in the best light, with attractive images and accurate details. However, There are a lot of problems that can occur during product photography. Manual shooting is time-consuming and can be expensive, mistakes are common, image quality can vary, and these issues can have a negative impact on sales. It is in this context that Orbitvu has established itself as an essential partner for brands such as Bosch, Clarks, Mercedes-Benz, Mercedes-Benz, Seiko, Chanel or even Jagermeister.Founded in 2004, this Polish company offers photography solutions of automated, efficient and high-quality products. In this article, we'll take a detailed look at why brands are increasingly looking to collaborate with Orbitvu to improve their product photography.

What are the common problems brands encounter when it comes to product photography?

The search for the right light

One of the most common issues you may encounter in product photography is difficulty getting good light. Indeed, to obtain professional quality photos, suitable lighting is essential, but it can quickly turn out to be a real headache...

‍

The settings required can be numerous and complex. : it is essential to precisely adjust the various lighting elements, such as the height and angle of the lights, their color temperature, their intensity, etc... And then take test photos to determine if these settings are the right ones or if they need to be adjusted. This problem also increases if the products you have to photograph are very different from each other. Your settings should in fact be modified according to the needs of each product, their shape, their color or even their texture. If you have the misfortune to switch from a very light or reflective product to a particularly dark product, for example, you will have to review your entire light profile. If you want to know more about the particularities of light in product photography, and more specifically the advantages of a toplight, we invite you to go consult our dedicated article.Adjusting the light alone can therefore take a considerable amount of time before you even start your product photography session...

Photo studio settings

While the light can be difficult to set, you can imagine that the same is true for your entire photo studio, from the placement of your product to that of the camera, including the choice of the background. This problem gets even worse if you want to go further than simple still photography: 360-degree animation can thus be a real challenge with a traditional photo studio, in the same way as video.Setting up all this equipment can be tedious and time-consuming., sometimes requiring hours of adjustments before you can start taking photos.

The significant loss of time on repetitive tasks during retouching

After product photography as such, comes the post-production retouching phase. If you are starting out with a professional studio or if you do not have the right equipment, you will often have to correct the lighting, color, composition, and contrast to do justice to your product. However, all these corrections take time and can often delay the uploading of your new product photos... In addition to retouching, you will often have to do other things further changes to the image, and the Clipping is a good example. It can in fact be a relatively easy task to do by hand with a simple tool like Photoroom if your product is not complex and has a good contrast between the background and the product itself in particular... But the Clipping is becoming particularly arduous on other products, like a white product on a white background! In these cases, more rudimentary tools like Photoroom are no longer enough, and professional paid tools require extensive knowledge to handle them, not to mention the surgical precision required. Moreover, whether we are talking about retouching or more advanced modifications, the fact remains that most of the tasks done in post-production will always be the same.

‍

‍

However, free software does not allow automate or to “batch” your tasks to save you time, while professional software like Photoshop will require a paid license, as well as a workforce trained in their use. You then end up either with a long list of repetitive tasks without any way of automating them (a harmful waste of time and productivity), either with a subscription to be paid every month and employees to be trained to use complex editing software. Fortunately, there is a third solution that greatly simplifies this process, from shooting to publishing, including all the retouching and modifications you may need, without a subscription to pay every month... But we'll tell you more about it later in this article.

The difficulty in ensuring continuity and homogeneity between all your photos

Without careful planning and execution, you may end up with a set of photos that lack harmony and coherence.The Variations in light can affect the color, saturation, and contrast of products, creating inconsistencies. This light can also have an impact on the background color, which can distract the customer's attention and distract them from the product. Framing is also important : if your products are not always placed in the same place in the frame, or at the same distance, this can also be particularly distracting for the customer, especially if we are on the same type of products (shoes for example).

‍

‍

It is therefore essential for you to Plan your product photography carefully. Before each shoot, you must ensure:

  • that the shooting parameters are consistent,
  • that the light is uniform,
  • that the backgrounds are the same,
  • and that the orientation and framing are in accordance with a predefined standard.

The need to have a solid knowledge of photography

To obtain professional quality photos, it is often necessary to have a solid knowledge of photography and to master your photo studio perfectly. Unfortunately, many companies do not have the in-house skills to take quality photographs of their products. It is for this reason that many brands use professional photographers, whether internal or external, but it can quickly represent a certain cost.

faqs.question: What are the main alternatives to Orbitvu Studios?
faqs.answer: Several solutions exist on the market, each with its own specificities. StyleShoots is often chosen for fashion and textiles, with automated models and lighting systems dedicated to this sector. PhotoRobot, for its part, offers motorized platforms adapted to 360 and 3D shots, although its software is more technical and requires more settings. Another alternative is Scancube, which uses compact lightboxes that allow images of small products to be captured on a white background, but with less flexibility.

faqs.question: What is the impact of AI on photo quality?
faqs.answer: Orbitvu's AI photo assistant automatically identifies the product and optimizes the lighting accordingly. The system of 74 controllable light panels ensures consistent professional quality, even for users without photography expertise.

faqs.question: Why are box-type solutions like Scancube less flexible?
faqs.answer: Camera boxes like those from Scancube are closed solutions, designed primarily for packshot photography of small objects. One of the main disadvantages of these systems is their fixed lighting, similar to the old Ortery series. Unlike Orbitvu studios, where light sources can be adjusted in intensity, color temperature and direction, the boxes impose predefined lighting that can only be changed by physically repositioning the product inside. This rigidity limits the possibilities of staging and can be a problem when you have to shoot products with complex textures, reflective surfaces or varied volumes. In addition, these boxes are often designed for neutral white backgrounds and do not allow you to manage more creative situations or lighting. 360° shooting is also more demanding, as these systems do not have integrated rotating platforms as advanced as those of Orbitvu. In comparison, an Orbitvu studio allows you to capture standardized visuals while offering great flexibility in settings and lighting.

faqs.question: What happens to PackshotCreator?
faqs.answer: PackshotCreator is no longer an alternative to Orbitvu since it is now the official distributor of Orbitvu solutions in France and French-speaking Europe. It is therefore no longer a competitor, but a key player in supporting and training companies wishing to automate their visual production with Orbitvu.

faqs.question: Can you use a traditional camera instead of an automated studio?
faqs.answer: It is entirely possible to opt for traditional equipment, such as a Canon, Nikon, or Fujifilm body, but this involves longer manual adjustments, a need for photographic expertise and a greater amount of post-production time. Unlike Orbitvu studios, these classic configurations do not allow for rapid standardization of visuals and often require extensive retouching before publication.
